title: Joy Fielding: The Transformation
text: Joy Fielding is a Canadian novelist and actress. She lives in Toronto, Ontario.

title: Farley Mowat: Canada North Now: The Great Betrayal
text: Farley McGill Mowat was a Canadian writer and environmentalist. His works were translated into 52 languages, and he sold more than 17 million books.

title: See 1976 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1976 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit was selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts.

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: Suzanne Martel
text: Suzanne Chouinard Martel was a French Canadian journalist, novelist and children's writer.

title: The Man Who Skied Down Everest becomes the first Canadian dramatic film to win an Academy Award
text: The Man Who Skied Down Everest is a Canadian documentary about Yuichiro Miura, a Japanese alpinist who skied down Mount Everest in 1970. It follows a Japanese expedition through the planning, preparation, and execution of a partial ascent and high-speed descent of Everest.

title: Second City Television premiers
text: Second City Television, commonly shortened to SCTV and later known as SCTV Network 90 and SCTV Channel (the Cinemax version), is a Canadian television sketch comedy show that ran intermittently between 1976 and 1984 about a fictional television station. It was created as an offshoot of Toronto's Second City troupe.

title: “You Sexy Thing” by Hot Chocolate
text: "You Sexy Thing" is a song by the British soul band Hot Chocolate. It was written by lead singer Errol Brown and bass guitarist Tony Wilson and was produced by Mickie Most.

title: “Love Hurts” by Nazareth
text: "Love Hurts" is a song written and composed by the American songwriter Boudleaux Bryant. First recorded by The Everly Brothers in July 1960, the song is best known in two hit versions by UK artists: by the Scottish hard rock band Nazareth for their 1975 LP Hair of the Dog and by the English singer-songwriter Jim Capaldi in 1975.

title: “Get Up and Boogie” by Silver Convention
text: "Get Up and Boogie" is a song by German disco act Silver Convention from their 1976 second album of the same name. The song was written and composed by Sylvester Levay and Stephan Prager, and produced by Prager.
